en: The *Mūlamandala-dhāraṇī Sūtra*,
translated by an unknown person, now appended to the Liang dynasty catalog:
If one wishes to receive and maintain the Mūlamandala and must achieve its efficacy, one must first protect the three [refuges].
One should cause one's karma to be utterly purified.
Furthermore, first selecting a stūpa containing some of the śarīra relics,
one should then choose an auspicious season, month, and day.
That which is called the "auspicious time" refers to the period from the first day to the fifteenth day of the waxing moon.
While it is also permissible to perform the rite on a single day,
the fifteenth day of that month is considered the most excellent.
Bathe with fragrant water and don fresh, clean garments.
According to one's means, make offerings to all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Vajras.
Light four lamps and take seasonal flowers as offerings.
One should consume the three kinds of white food.
Every day, one should circumambulate the stūpa and the maṇḍala;
for each circuit walked, one should recite [the mantra] once.
Having thus completed one hundred and eight recitations,
if sleep should come, simply sleep before the stūpa.
At the break of dawn, the Buddha and Vajrapāṇi will appear within your dreams.
Once this response has been obtained, whatever vows one may have will all be fulfilled without exception.
Furthermore, if one recites this dhāraṇī thirty thousand times,
even the grave sins of the five heinous acts will be immediately eliminated.
If one upholds this dhāraṇī seeking its manifest efficacy,
one must not harbor any covetous thoughts; rather,
one should remain free from the defilement of desire and maintain a single-minded resolve.
Reciting and upholding it in this manner will bring swift efficacy without exception.
If one can recite it one hundred and eight times each day,
there will be nothing one undertakes that does not yield benefit.
One cannot be harmed by any poisons;
even when others employ sorcery or toxic spells, one remains unharmed.
Water cannot drown or sweep one away, and fire cannot burn.
They shall not be defiled by diseases or epidemics;
even should there be any internal threats from bandits or calamities, they shall not cause harm.
Furthermore, it shall enable the eyes, ears, nose, and other faculties [to function].
Furthermore, there shall be no pain in the mouth, teeth, or any part of the body;
nor shall they be afflicted by fevers or other ailments for even one, two, or three days.
No venomous serpents or wild beasts shall ever again cause them harm, nor can any malevolent spells or sorcery ever inflict injury upon them.
In short, no evil whatsoever shall be able to prevail against them.
One should know that this maṇḍala possesses such great majestic power and spiritual efficacy that it can eliminate all matters of fear and destroy all root transgressions.
It is able to abide in all dwellings of merit;
it is able to fulfill all practices of the pāramitās;
and it can even cause one to swiftly reach unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
If one recites this atop a high mountain peak,
all sentient beings dwelling in the valleys, waters, and lands—
whether within the range of sight or seeing the mantra-reciter— [shall be affected].
All those various species will exhaust their karmic retributions and shall never again fall into the three evil realms.
If one recites this mantra within a celestial temple, [the same result shall follow].
All the yakṣa deities will come to pay their respects.
If one recites this mantra within a pond inhabited by nāgas,
all the nāgas will come to pay their respects.
If one recites this mantra before sunrise,
Surīrāja will descend and pay respectful homage.
If one recites this mantra before an image of Vajra, [the same shall occur].
The Vajra-body will manifest and fulfill one's wishes.
If one recites the mantra over achyranthes (chángpú) eight thousand times and consumes it oneself,
one will see King Hiraṇyakaśipu.
Whatever one says will not be contradicted by anyone.
If one recites this mantra over eight thousand grains of black pepper and holds them in the mouth,
it will cause all who see one to rejoice.
Whomever they command or instruct will not dare to disobey.
If one recites the mantra over white mustard seeds eight thousand times and scatters them into the air,
it can cause fierce winds and torrential rains [to cease].
Unseasonable frost, hail, and all such calamities will be entirely extinguished.
If one recites this mantra over salt eight hundred times and then consumes it with *baramī*, [the aforementioned effects will be achieved].
It can cause those of evil intent among the non-Buddhists to have their malice spontaneously extinguished and to all come to seek refuge and serve [the practitioner].
If one recites the mantra over white mustard seeds while calling upon the name of a king, [the same result will follow].
Having recited the mantra one hundred and eight times for each incense offering,
one will be able to cause the rāja to submit and follow along, no longer acting in opposition.
If one recites the mantra over eight thousand offerings of *agaru* (aloe) incense...
When this is burned and its smoke reaches one afflicted by a spirit-disease,
that spirit immediately reveals its own name.
The incantation-master then rebukes and dispatches the spirit, which has no choice but to comply.
If one wishes to pray for rain,
take the mud from the dung of a green ox and fashion a dragon with three heads;
dye its back and spine vermilion and adorn its chest with gold.
First, construct a square altar;
whether on a raised platform or level ground, it may be made at any time.
Furthermore, paint the altar with blue and green colors.
Upon the altar, place a dragon.
At each of the four corners of the altar, set one water jar and one incense burner;
in one burner, burn aloeswood incense, and in the other, burn sandalwood incense.
Burn one portion of blended incense with clarified butter and one portion of guggulu incense.
Furthermore, outside the main altar,
construct another altar measuring four cubits in length and breadth, smeared with cow dung.
Place vases at the four corners:
one filled with water mixed with milk, one filled with water mixed with curd,
and one filled with water mixed with milk-gruel.
First, fill [the vessels] with water and fat.
Furthermore, light eight lamps within the maṇḍala.
Additionally, firmly press down the feet [of the figures], and adorn the maṇḍala with *kusumbha* flowers—this refers to red-blue flowers—and with parched grain flour.
Furthermore, insert an arrow at each of the four corners.
Then, encircle the arrows with thread of five colors.
Additionally, fashion small banners of five colors and suspend them from the tips of the arrows.
Furthermore, scatter seven kinds of grain within the altar and use five colors to adorn and provide offerings upon it.
Additionally, place all various flowers and fruits available at that time entirely within the altar.
Thereupon, the mantra-master faces east,
consecrates eight thousand grains of white mustard seed,
and strikes the head of the dragon with them once for each recitation of the mantra.
When the mantra has been recited eight thousand times in this manner,
great clouds will gather from all four directions and sweet rain will pour down.
From that time forward, all nāgas shall pay them full respect and veneration.
If the rain is excessive, recite the mantra over white mustard seeds eight hundred times and cast them into water where dragons dwell; the rain will immediately cease.
While reciting this mantra, one must not speak at all.
If, when praying for rain, swift clouds, violent winds, bitter mist,
or sudden hail gather and disperse intermittently, obstructing the rain,
one should fashion stakes from khadira wood and strike them into the shore of the dragon’s abyss.
Then all obstacles and difficulties will completely disperse.
Should there be any obstacles at the time of praying for rain that prevent the rain from falling, [this shall likewise resolve them].
Within the mandala, one should draw a *vināyaka* sword.
Take eight hundred grains of white mustard seed;
recite the mantra over each grain once and strike the *vināyaka* sword with them.
Having thus completed eight hundred recitations,
it will cause all those who create obstacles and difficulties to be spontaneously bound,
so that they can no longer obstruct the rain, which shall then fall.
Once the rite is completed, one should wash away the painted image using breast milk.
Vīṇāyudha will be exceedingly joyful,
and from that time forward, all that is sought shall be accomplished without fail.
The body and clothing of the mantra-practitioner must always be solemn, pure, and clean.
Such is a brief explanation of the merits of the fundamental maṇḍala.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:

*Tadyathā | sarvatathāgatānām oṃ vibhūṣitavijayamaṇiprabhe tathāgatadharṣaṇi maṇe maṇe suprabhe vimale saṃkramaṇi bhaṭṭārike hūṃ hūṃ śvare śvare buddhavilokite khāhi khāhi jaye tiṣṭha vijaye svāhā*. This is the fundamental dhāraṇī method.
Furthermore, the merits of the Great Maṇḍala of Mūli shall now be explained.
One who completes one hundred thousand recitations will behold all the Buddhas;
one who completes two hundred thousand recitations—
One who attains the vision of all the stages of bodhisattva practice and completes three hundred thousand recitations is as if they have already entered all maṇḍalas.
One who maintains all mantras and achieves success in them without exception, having recited [this mantra] four hundred thousand times,
shall become a king among all mantra-holders.
One who has recited it five hundred thousand times, [shall likewise attain such status].
One who has recited it six million times will be able to see all the palaces and abodes of the asuras,
and will obtain the sight of all hidden treasures beneath the earth.
One who completes seven hundred thousand recitations shall perceive the fundamental source of all events in the present and the future.
One who completes eight hundred thousand recitations...
This person shall attain the Treasure-Ocean Samādhi.
One who completes ninety million recitations will attain the true practice and right action of all Buddhas and tread upon the ground of wondrous enlightenment.
One who completes one million recitations shall receive the prediction of enlightenment from all Buddhas.
Even if a person has committed the five heinous crimes of immediate retribution and other such sins, [they shall be purified].
One who can recite this mantra one hundred thousand times shall have all such grave offenses as described above completely extinguished,
and shall attain the stage of non-retrogression.
Furthermore, he attains knowledge of the good and evil thoughts of all others.

He also attains the purification of the faculty of the eye, the purification of the faculty of the ear, the purification of the faculty of the nose, the purification of the faculty of the tongue, and the purification of the faculty of the body.
Adorned by the karma of the purification of the five faculties,
whoever recites this mantra one hundred thousand times shall obtain the merits as described above.
The aforementioned inexhaustible grave offenses are extinguished;
as for reaching one million recitations,
two hundred thousand are contained within each of those [sections].
One shall further obtain immeasurable and boundless merit;
each individual merit shall be twice as superior as the preceding one.
Furthermore, one should first bathe and don new, clean garments.
Take one *hūda* (Sanskrit: *sūkṣma-kaṇḍa*, the meaning of which is uncertain) and grind it with water inside a copper vessel.
Place it before the Buddha and offer the "three white foods."
From the eighth day to the fifteenth day,
if one recites and maintains this mantra for a full hundred thousand times,
Sūryadeva shall manifest three signs in the present.
If one takes the "warm" sign and applies it to the forehead,
one will arrive at whatever destination one intends to go. Furthermore,
among all kings, one shall be regarded as a sovereign through the power of this mantra.
Furthermore, recite the mantra again while waiting for the appearance of smoke on the forehead; as soon as it appears,
take the *kheṭa* from the forehead and apply it to the eyes.
Instantly, one will see all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Vajradharas dwelling in the ten directions;
and no demons whatsoever will dare to cast an evil eye upon this person.
All essential dharmas are entirely perfected;
all merits are fully accomplished without exception.
Furthermore, the appearance of fire upon his forehead signifies this.
Then one attains the *śavara-nirgama-samādhi*,
whereby one obtains great majesty and all-encompassing sovereignty among the Heaven of the Thirty-three.
Furthermore, if one recites it ten thousand times on a mountain peak,
one will attain great preeminence among all the clans throughout the regions of Jambudvīpa and proceed to the rank of a kṣatriya king.
If one enters into water inhabited by nāgas and recites [the mantra] eight thousand times,
all nāgas will not fail to show reverence.
If one consecrates white mustard seeds with the mantra eight thousand times, [the same result shall follow].
If scattered into the air, it can cause rain to fall.
All nāgas shall respectfully obey [this person] if they can recite and maintain this mantra every day;
the merit and karmic fruit of such a person are inconceivable and beyond description.
Furthermore, take a new, clean jar and fill it with pure water.
Then, according to the local terrain, collect various flowers, grasses, and trees,
taking only their tender, soft sprouts and placing them all inside the jar.
Furthermore, take indrahāse-duḥ (ginseng, resembling a hand), unascertained *kṣemaka* (*khemaka*), white mustard seeds (*siddhārthaka*), *utpala* flowers, and sandalwood.
With these and other such superior medicinal substances,
place them all within water and recite the mantra ten thousand times.
If there are all manner of evil ailments and pains among people in the world, [they shall be cured].
One should take it as medicine and also use it for bathing;
all who are ill will be completely cured,
and all transgressions will be entirely extinguished.
It shall also cause all curses and sorcery performed by wicked persons to be naturally extinguished.
Furthermore, it shall cause all people to give rise to reverence.
This is due to the power of this mantra and medicine.
It can cause such a person to possess great majestic power.
If one suffers from white leprosy or various other forms of leprosy,
they should drink this water and also bathe with it.
These various malignant diseases will be immediately cured.
If there are women who have been unable to give birth since their youth,
by drinking this medicinal water and bathing with it, they will immediately be able to give birth.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who encounters all manner of inauspiciousness,
whose endeavors are always frustrated, and who lacks constant blessings and protection—
if such a person drinks this medicinal water or bathes with it— [they shall be purified].
Whatever one directs toward it will accord with one's wishes; there is nothing that does not harmonize with the mind.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke thus regarding the merits of the *citta-dhāraṇī*, and then he uttered the mantra, which says:
Oṃ maṇivajre hūṃ phaṭ. Furthermore, the mantra according to the heart-essence is as follows:
Oṃ maṇidhare hūṃ phaṭ. Next, the merits of the Upāra-mahāmaṇḍala shall be explained.
If one recites this ten thousand times,
it will cause all the Vīṇā-yakṣas, sword-bearing māras, their retinues, and malevolent spirits and ghosts to bow down in submission.
The mantra-practitioner places his chest upon the ground at the feet [of the deity],
seeking mercy and begging for life, and all together they chant:
"We respectfully receive and comply with all your instructions."
If one recites it twenty-one thousand times,
one will attain preeminence among all the devas; furthermore,
all the nāgas and others will come to seek refuge, pay homage, serve, and obey one's commands.
If one recites it thirty thousand times,
all yakṣas and all malevolent spirits will without exception show respect and obedience, submitting and serving them.
If one recites it fifty thousand times,
whatever matters one desires— regardless of whether they are far or near—
will be accomplished according to one's wishes as soon as they are undertaken.
Within that desire realm, among all classes of sentient beings including the asuras,
everything they do according to their will is met with faith and compliance.
If one recites this eight thousand times,
all the Vajras, their retinues, and their various tribes will stand before that person and respectfully await their instructions.
If one recites it ninety thousand times,
all bodhisattvas will joyfully protect and mindfully attend to them.
If one recites it one hundred thousand times, [the same shall occur].
All Buddhas appeared before him in person and addressed him,
saying: "O son of good family,
all your aspirations shall now be fulfilled."
You may go at your will to the pure lands of the ten directions.
All dhāraṇīs and mantras, as well as all dharmas,
you have already fully mastered.
We, all the Buddhas,
shall now bestow upon you the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
All virtues and all fruits of retribution are now fully perfected within you.
The merits of the great Utpala-maṇḍala are thus to be understood according to their sequence. Thereupon,
he spoke the mantra:
6. The Seat-Mantra (Āsana-mantra). All editions lack the numbering above this point. Oṃ maṇi-kumtari hūṃ hūṃ svāhā. This is called the Seat-Mantra.

7. The Mantra for Binding the Mandala. Furthermore, the mantra for binding the mandala is: Oṃ maṇivijaye dhara dhara hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. When binding the mandala, one should recite this mantra immediately.
Recite the mantra over white mustard seeds seven times and scatter them within the maṇḍala.

8. The Mantra for Binding the Boundaries of the Ten Directions. Furthermore, the mantra for binding the boundaries of the ten directions is: Oṃ śvadhūḥ kṛtamaṇi ruṭi riṇi huṃ huṃ phaṭ phaṭ (with the final *phaṭ* uttered with half a syllable). When binding the boundaries, [recite this].
Take white mustard seeds and sprinkle them with scented water after reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times;
this will bind the ten directions and establish a boundary.

9. The Mantra for Binding All Vināyakas. Furthermore, the mantra for binding all Vināyakas: Oṃ maṇi vara vara vāni hana hana huṃ phaṭ phaṭ (half-sound) svāhā. If there are those who create obstacles and difficulties, such as the Vināyakas...
Take ashes and mix them with water; recite the mantra twenty-one times and scatter them throughout the ten directions.
This will cause all Vināyakas to be completely bound, so that none shall be able to create obstacles or difficulties.

10. The Mantra for Binding and Protecting the Body. Furthermore, the mantra for binding and protecting the body is: *Oṃ vajramaṇi tiṣṭha tiṣṭha hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ*. If one wishes to protect the body, [one should recite this].
Recite the mantra seventeen times with both hands and rub them upon one’s head.

11. The Mantra for Binding Clean Clothes: Next is the mantra for binding clean clothes. (1) Oṃ (2) maṇivibhūṣi (3) jili jili (4) huṃ phaṭ. 12. The Mantra for Washing Hands and Face: Next is the mantra for washing hands and face. (1) Oṃ vidyuvate hara hara mahāmaṇi huṃ huṃ phaṭ. When washing hands or face:
Chant the mantra over water to wash one’s hands and face, and sprinkle it all over the body.
13. The Mantra for Bathing. Furthermore, the bathing mantra: *Oṃ sunirmala-vati hara hara pāpam hūṃ hūṃ svāhā*. When performing the bath, [recite this].
Take white mustard seeds and mix them with pure water; recite the mantra one hundred and eight times and bathe the body with it.

Regarding those who wish to establish a maṇḍala, the ritual application of the cubit measurement is as follows:
first, one must select the site before beginning the construction of the maṇḍala.
The maṇḍala shall have four gates opened.
Finely grind the five-colored earth into powder and place it in new earthenware vessels,
each containing sandalwood and musk.
Having applied [the ointment], place it within the altar.
Furthermore, take two earthenware vessels:
in one, place fine sandalwood powder; in the other, place *campaka* flowers.
Use the five colors previously mentioned to delineate the altar.
Construct the central altar to be two cubits square;
smear it with white sandalwood and scatter saffron powder upon it.
Outside that altar, extending further to the west,
mark out separate areas each measuring fourteen cubits;
smear the ground with pure earth mixed with cow dung.
The central altar shall be made with seven colors;
one should paint a lotus flower adorned with the seven treasures,
and upon that flower, paint a thousand-spoked wheel with its rim.
The outer perimeter of the wheel is entirely fashioned as flames.
The lotus stalk is made in the form of vaidūrya gemstone.
Upon it, the Buddha is fashioned.
To the left of the Buddha, depict Vajrapāṇi;
his right hand holds a vajra and his left hand grasps a battle-axe (paraśu).
To the right of the Buddha, depict the Bodhisattva Maṇibhadra.
His body is adorned with various kinds of necklaces and ornaments;
one hand holds a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*), and the other hand grasps a *akṣamālā* rosary. In the four corner positions, the Four Heavenly Kings (*Caturmahārāja*) are depicted.
The body is adorned with various ornaments such as armor and necklaces,
and its majestic deportment may take a formidable form.
Before the altar is constructed, there are inner and outer altars.
First, one should excavate and remove one cubit of the inferior soil.
The center of the altar should be made slightly elevated.
Furthermore, it must be adorned with banners, flags, and canopies suspended and erected.
One should use five colors to paint the four borders of the altar.
Outside the altar, construct a fire pit in each of the four directions, using fine firewood and kindling the fires according to the ritual rules.
At each of the four corners of the pits, install banners and streamers.
Five-colored silks and brocades surround the altar on all sides;
a single gate is left on the southern side for entry and exit.
At each of the outer corners of the altar, banners and streamers are placed facing east.
Furthermore, mix five kinds of incense with water and place it in a golden flask;
set a beautiful flower in each and position them at the corners of the altar.
If a golden flask is unavailable, one may also use small earthenware flasks coated with gold.
Furthermore, place four silver vases, each filled to the brim with milk, at the four corners.
Outside the gate of the central altar, on the right side,
paint Mahādeva and Vemacitrin together in one place.
Adorned with various kinds of necklaces and ornaments,
in the middle of the left gate, one should paint Śaṅkhinī;
in the center of the third gate, one should paint Vajradūtī.
He has eight arms, each hand grasping a distinct weapon;
his body is adorned with various kinds of necklaces and ornaments,
and he raises both hands high above his head.
In the petition submitted by Zhang Qingjuan,
it states that on all four sides of the central altar,
various kinds of colorful and exquisite foods and drinks were used as offerings.
Furthermore, fill four vases with scented water and insert fine flowers into each;
place them near the deities at the four corners and light thirty-two lamps.
Upon a lotus flower in the center of the mandala, place a single golden flask filled with scented water.
Place various fruits and various grains and cereals within it,
and also insert various flowers therein as an offering to the Buddha.
One should burn ghee and blended incense before the Buddha;
for all other positions, each should burn their own respective incense.
A silver incense burner is to be placed before the Buddha on the central altar.
Before Vajrapāṇi, burn kuru-kuru and dhūpa; before Aniximaṇi-vajrī, burn tuṣka-ga incense; and before the Four Heavenly Kings, burn incense of frankincense (kunduruka).
Burn *sāccha* incense and *tuka* incense together;
burn white sandalwood incense before Mahādevī,
and burn *guggulu* incense before Śaṅkhinī.
At the base of the altar, the messenger should first separately burn *lākṣā* incense.
At the gates of the central mandala, various offerings should be placed separately at each one.
At the eastern gate, draw *Aridi* (pronounced with the "ding-li" rhyme) together with her six sisters.
On the right, the western side,
paint Mahādeva and Puṣpadanta; on the northern side,
paint Vemacitrin with an expression of bashfulness.
Thirty-two arrows are to be inserted along the four sides of the altar.
These are encircled with threads of five colors.
At the four corners of this place, five-colored silk banners must be installed.
Scatter various kinds of flowers randomly upon the altar.
Place various mixed fruits there as an offering.
Furthermore, prepare seven types of cakes, adorning the surface of each cake with various delicious flavors.

one hundred and eight lamps;

furthermore, before each of the devas,

of these, eight jars were filled with the milk gruel.

Each of these four types of beverages was likewise contained in eight jars.

boil them together to make gruel and place it in eight vessels.

four bowls filled with sesame oil and four bowls filled with high-quality clarified butter (*ghṛta*).

On each side of the entrance, place one *kamaṇḍalu* (water jar), filled with scented water, and consecrate it by reciting this mantra:

Oṃ mahā-vipula-paśyati-tuṣṭita-siddhi-bhisma-mānaka-sarva-tathāgata-viśodhaya sphara sphara sa-phara hūṃ hūṃ. Furthermore, one should know that all items intended for entry into the maṇḍala—such as incense, flowers, food and drink, fruits, and clothing—[should be prepared accordingly].
Even for ashes, soil, water, fire, or any other such substances,
one must first recite this mantra over water and sprinkle it upon them before bringing them inside.
If one invites the Buddha, the deities, and the Four Heavenly Kings to be seated upon their thrones,
each should be invited and established using the respective body-seal (kāyamudrā) and its fundamental mantra.
Once the construction of the central altar is completed:
Immediately, one should invite the Bodhisattvas and Vajras;
each one should be firmly established upon their seat with its own body-seal and root mantra.
Having invited them, one must withdraw and may not step upon them again.
Once the inner maṇḍala has been completed, one should then construct the outer maṇḍala.
When the seating for all has been arranged, one should immediately recite mantras over one’s own seat and bind protection for oneself.
If others are to be led into the maṇḍala, [the same procedure applies].
First, have them wash their clothes and bathe, and provide each with the purification ritual (*kṣānti*).
Lead them to the side of the furnace and have them sit down in succession.
Furthermore, one should know that if they approach with a sincere heart and rely upon the instructions, [the rite will succeed].
If one who is fully endowed with the Dharma merely enters this maṇḍala once with a sincere heart,
all the Buddhas of the ten directions [will acknowledge them].
They shall likewise bestow upon this person the prediction of purity.
All grave offenses of the past and present will be entirely extinguished.
If one is afflicted by sorcery or malevolent spirits that ought to be destroyed, [this shall effect their dissolution].
All obstacles and difficulties shall be entirely eliminated.
Those suffering from serious illnesses will be cured as soon as they enter this maṇḍala.
Even those possessed by any kind of ghost or spirit will be liberated from their affliction immediately upon entering this maṇḍala.
If one wishes to make offerings to all Buddhas of the ten directions;
if one wishes to make offerings to all Bodhisattvas;
or if one wishes to attain the seeds of Buddha-wisdom and deeply plant the root of Bodhi.
If one desires to be firm and non-retrogressive,
one should enter this dharma-maṇḍala according to the instructions.
If one desires to make offerings throughout to the Mahādeva, Maheśvara, Nārāyaṇa, Brahmā, Śakra, and the thirty-two honored deities, [one should do so here].
If one simply makes a single offering according to this mandala,
it is as if each and every deity has been individually worshipped;
consequently, all the deities will be completely delighted.
If one makes a single offering to this maṇḍala,
it is as if one were making offerings to the five brothers, the Mahākāla-pañcaka, and the seven sisters, the Kheṭakā-saptaka.
And having completed the offerings to the Four Heavenly Kings, the thirty-two Mātṛdāhas, and all the other devas as prescribed,
one should further know that once this maṇḍala has been constructed:
Whether one seeks to fulfill a wish by petitioning a Buddha,
or by petitioning a Bodhisattva,
or by petitioning any of the aforementioned devas.
All shall fully accomplish every fruit and vow;
as stated above, there is nothing that cannot be attained.
Should one encounter calamities or have an unstable life-span, [this practice shall bring peace].
It is difficult to obtain rare treasures through ordinary means; however,
for one who has entered this maṇḍala, all matters and intentions will be entirely auspicious and fulfilled according to their wishes.
If calamities and epidemics spread within the country,
and the poisonous vapors of evil spirits and demons abound,
by establishing an altar and making offerings, the disasters and illnesses will be extinguished.
If a king fears the envoys of neighboring enemies,
once he has established this Dharma, all hostile marauders will spontaneously submit;
by the power of this merit, none shall cause him harm.
Whether seeking fame and official rank, or seeking wealth and abundance, those who establish this altar shall have all their wishes fulfilled.
If one can enter this altar with utmost sincerity,
they shall attain freedom from illness in this very lifetime.
No malevolent spirits or ghosts shall find an opportunity to harm them;
they shall always be admired and praised by all,
their every aim shall accord with their wishes, and all people shall revere and submit to them.
Esteemed by all and universally trusted,
one shall obtain supreme benefit and merit at all times and in all places;
and after casting off this body, in every place of rebirth, [one shall continue to attain such excellence].
From one buddha-field to another buddha-field,
they always sit upon jeweled flowers before the Buddhas,
fully accomplishing all the practices of the Buddhas.
Before long, one shall attain the Way that is peerless and unequaled.
